subject: maths
title: Year 4 Counting by Fractions and Mixed Numerals
seo_title: Year 4 Counting by Fractions Worksheets: Mixed Numerals and Number Lines (Free, with Answer Key)
standard_text: Count by fractions including mixed numerals; locate and represent these fractions as numbers on number lines
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on counting by fractions for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M4N04): count on and back by halves, thirds, quarters and fifths, improper fractions, mixed numerals, number lines from 0 to 3 and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Count on by the same fraction each time. After 3/4 comes 4/4 = 1, then 1 1/4.
key_sub: A mixed numeral like 1 1/4 is 1 whole and 1 quarter (not 1.4). On a number line, go to 1, then count on 1 quarter mark.
body_html:
Counting by fractions

Counting by quarters means adding 14 each time. After 34 comes 44, which is 1 whole. Then keep going: 1 14, 1 24 …

Example

Count on by thirds from 13 to 2.

Add 13 each time. 33 = 1 and 1 33 = 2.

Answer: 13, 23, 1, 1 13, 1 23, 2

Example

Count back by halves from 2 12.

Take away 12 each time. One half less than 2 is 1 12.

Answer: 2 12, 2, 1 12, 1, 12

Improper fractions and mixed numerals

An improper fraction such as 74 has a numerator bigger than its denominator. A mixed numeral such as 1 34 shows the same amount as wholes and a fraction.

Example

Write 2 13 as an improper fraction.

2 wholes = 2 × 3 = 6 thirds. Add 1 third: 6 + 1 = 7.

Answer: 73

Mixed numerals on a number line

Find the whole number first. Then count on the marks for the fraction part.

Example

Where is 2 23 on a number line split into thirds?

Go to 2. Each mark is 13, so count on 2 marks.

Answer: 2 marks after 2, just before 3

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
34, 45, …Add 14 each time. The denominator stays 4: 34, 1, 1 14
Skipping the whole: 34, 1 1444 = 1 comes first: 34, 1, 1 14
Putting 1 14 at 1.41 14 is 1 whole and 1 quarter: 1 quarter mark after 1. (It is 1.25, not 1.4.)
Counting all the parts in all the bars for the denominator: 78The denominator is the number of parts in one whole: 74

faq.q: What do Year 4 students learn about counting by fractions?
faq.a: In the Australian Curriculum (AC9M4N04), Year 4 students count by fractions such as quarters, thirds, halves and fifths, including mixed numerals, and show these numbers on a number line. For example: 1/4, 2/4, 3/4, 1, 1 1/4.
A mixed numeral is a whole number and a fraction written together, such as 1 3/4. It is the same amount as the improper fraction 7/4, because 1 whole is 4 quarters and 4 + 3 = 7.

faq.q: How do you put a mixed numeral on a number line?
faq.a: Go to the whole number first, then count on the fraction part. For 2 1/3 on a line split into thirds, go to 2 and count 1 more mark.
No. 1 1/4 is 1 whole and 1 quarter, which is 1.25. 1.4 is 1 whole and 4 tenths, so 1 1/4 is less than 1.4.

sets.title: Count on by halves, thirds, quarters and fifths

items.q: Count on by quarters. Which number goes where the ? is?
items.e: Count on by quarters: each number is 14 more than the one before. 24 + 14 = 34.

items.q: Count on by quarters. Which number goes where the ? is?
items.e: Count on by quarters: each number is 14 more than the one before. 34 + 14 = 1. 4 quarters make 1 whole, so after 34 comes 1. Do not skip 1.

items.q: Count on by halves. Which number goes where the ? is?
items.e: Count on by halves: each number is 12 more than the one before. 1 + 12 = 1 12.

items.q: Count on by thirds. Which number goes where the ? is?
items.e: Count on by thirds: each number is 13 more than the one before. 1 + 13 = 1 13.

items.q: Count on by fifths. Which number goes where the ? is?
items.e: Count on by fifths: each number is 15 more than the one before. 45 + 15 = 1. 5 fifths make 1 whole, so after 45 comes 1. Do not skip 1.

items.q: Count on by quarters. Which number goes where the ? is?
items.e: Count on by quarters: each number is 14 more than the one before. 1 14 + 14 = 1 24.

items.q:
Count on by halves. What is the missing number?
12, 1, ?, 2
items.e: Count on by halves: each number is 12 more than the one before. 1 + 12 = 1 12.

items.q:
Count on by thirds. What is the missing number?
13, 23, ?, 1 13
items.e: Count on by thirds: each number is 13 more than the one before. 23 + 13 = 1. 3 thirds make 1 whole, so after 23 comes 1. Do not skip 1.

items.q:
Count on by quarters. What is the missing number?
24, 34, 1, ?
items.e: Count on by quarters: each number is 14 more than the one before. 1 + 14 = 1 14.

items.q:
Count on by fifths. What is the missing number?
25, 35, ?, 1
items.e: Count on by fifths: each number is 15 more than the one before. 35 + 15 = 45.

items.q:
Count on by fifths. What is the missing number?
45, ?, 1 15, 1 25
items.e: Count on by fifths: each number is 15 more than the one before. 45 + 15 = 1. 5 fifths make 1 whole, so after 45 comes 1. Do not skip 1.

items.q:
Count on by quarters. What is the missing number?
1 14, 1 24, ?, 2
items.e: Count on by quarters: each number is 14 more than the one before. 1 24 + 14 = 1 34.

items.q:
Count on by thirds. What is the missing number?
1, 1 13, 1 23, ?
items.e: Count on by thirds: each number is 13 more than the one before. 1 23 + 13 = 2. 3 thirds make 1 whole, so after 1 23 comes 2. Do not skip 2.

items.q:
Count on by halves. What is the missing number?
1 12, ?, 2 12, 3
items.e: Count on by halves: each number is 12 more than the one before. 1 12 + 12 = 2. 2 halves make 1 whole, so after 1 12 comes 2. Do not skip 2.

items.q: Count by quarters from 0. How many quarters make 1 whole?
items.e: 1 whole = 44 = 4 quarters.

items.q: Count by thirds from 0. How many thirds make 2?
items.e: 1 whole = 33, so 2 wholes = 2 × 3 = 6 thirds.

items.q: Count by halves from 0. How many halves make 2 12?
items.e: 1 whole = 22, so 2 wholes = 2 × 2 = 4 halves. Add 1 half more: 4 + 1 = 5.

items.q: Count by fifths from 0. How many fifths make 1 15?
items.e: 1 whole = 55 = 5 fifths. Add 1 fifth more: 5 + 1 = 6.

items.q: Count by quarters from 0. How many quarters make 1 34?
items.e: 1 whole = 44 = 4 quarters. Add 3 quarters more: 4 + 3 = 7.

items.q: Count by thirds from 0. How many thirds make 2 23?
items.e: 1 whole = 33, so 2 wholes = 2 × 3 = 6 thirds. Add 2 thirds more: 6 + 2 = 8.

sets.title: What comes next in a fraction count?

items.q:
Count on by quarters. What comes next?
1 14, 1 24, 1 34, ?
items.e: Count on by quarters: each number is 14 more than the one before. 1 34 + 14 = 2. 4 quarters make 1 whole, so after 1 34 comes 2. Do not skip 2.

items.q:
Count on by thirds. What comes next?
1 23, 2, 2 13, ?
items.e: Count on by thirds: each number is 13 more than the one before. 2 13 + 13 = 2 23.

items.q:
Count on by fifths. What comes next?
1 25, 1 35, 1 45, ?
items.e: Count on by fifths: each number is 15 more than the one before. 1 45 + 15 = 2. 5 fifths make 1 whole, so after 1 45 comes 2. Do not skip 2.

items.q:
Count on by halves. What comes next?
1 12, 2, 2 12, ?
items.e: Count on by halves: each number is 12 more than the one before. 2 12 + 12 = 3. 2 halves make 1 whole, so after 2 12 comes 3. Do not skip 3.

items.q:
Count on by quarters. What comes next?
2 14, 2 24, 2 34, ?
items.e: Count on by quarters: each number is 14 more than the one before. 2 34 + 14 = 3. 4 quarters make 1 whole, so after 2 34 comes 3. Do not skip 3.

items.q:
Count on by fifths. What comes next?
2 25, 2 35, 2 45, ?
items.e: Count on by fifths: each number is 15 more than the one before. 2 45 + 15 = 3. 5 fifths make 1 whole, so after 2 45 comes 3. Do not skip 3.

items.q:
Count back by quarters. What comes next?
1 24, 1 14, 1, ?
items.e: Count back by quarters: each number is 14 less than the one before. 1 − 14 = 34. One quarter less than 1 is 34.

items.q:
Count back by thirds. What comes next?
1 23, 1 13, 1, ?
items.e: Count back by thirds: each number is 13 less than the one before. 1 − 13 = 23. One third less than 1 is 23.

items.q:
Count back by halves. What comes next?
3, 2 12, 2, ?
items.e: Count back by halves: each number is 12 less than the one before. 2 − 12 = 1 12. One half less than 2 is 1 12.

items.q:
Count back by fifths. What comes next?
1 25, 1 15, 1, ?
items.e: Count back by fifths: each number is 15 less than the one before. 1 − 15 = 45. One fifth less than 1 is 45.

items.q:
Count back by quarters. What comes next?
2 24, 2 14, 2, ?
items.e: Count back by quarters: each number is 14 less than the one before. 2 − 14 = 1 34. One quarter less than 2 is 1 34.

items.q: Which shows counting on by quarters correctly?
c: 24, 34, 1, 2
24, 34, 45, 1
24, 34, 1 14, 1 24
24, 34, 1, 1 14
items.e: 24, 34, 1, 1 14. After 34 comes 44 = 1, then 1 14. 45 is not the next number, and 1 must not be skipped.

items.q: Which shows counting on by thirds correctly?
c: 1 13, 1 23, 1 34, 2
1 13, 1 23, 2, 2 13
1 13, 1 23, 2 13, 2 23
1 13, 1 23, 2, 3
items.e: 1 13, 1 23, 2, 2 13. After 1 23 comes 1 33 = 2, then 2 13. Each step is only 13.

items.q: Which shows counting on by fifths correctly?
c: 35, 45, 1 15, 1 25
35, 45, 56, 1
35, 45, 1, 1 15
35, 45, 1, 2
items.e: 35, 45, 1, 1 15. After 45 comes 55 = 1, then 1 15. The denominator stays 5.

items.q: Which shows counting back by halves correctly?
c: 2 12, 2, 1 12, 1
2 12, 2, 1, 12
2 12, 2, 1 12, 1 14
2 12, 1 12, 1, 12
items.e: 2 12, 2, 1 12, 1. Take away 12 each time: 2 12, 2, 1 12, 1. One half less than 2 is 1 12, not 1.

items.q: Start at 23. Count on 4 thirds. Where do you land?
items.e: Count on 4 steps of 13: 1, 1 13, 1 23, 2. You land on 2. Do not count the start number.

items.q: Start at 1 14. Count on 3 quarters. Where do you land?
items.e: Count on 3 steps of 14: 1 24, 1 34, 2. You land on 2. Do not count the start number.

items.q: Start at 35. Count on 4 fifths. Where do you land?
items.e: Count on 4 steps of 15: 45, 1, 1 15, 1 25. You land on 1 25. Do not count the start number.

items.q: Isla counts by fifths: 35, 45, 55. What is another way to write 55?
items.e: 5 fifths make 1 whole, so 55 = 1.

items.q: Counting by quarters, Jack says 2 24. Which number is the same as 2 24?
items.e: 24 is the same as 12, so 2 24 = 2 12.

sets.title: Improper fractions and mixed numerals from pictures

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Which improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is cut into 4 equal parts, so each part is 14. Count the shaded parts: 7. So it is 74. The denominator is the number of parts in one whole, not in all the bars.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Which improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is cut into 3 equal parts, so each part is 13. Count the shaded parts: 5. So it is 53. The denominator is the number of parts in one whole, not in all the bars.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Which improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is cut into 2 equal parts, so each part is 12. Count the shaded parts: 5. So it is 52. The denominator is the number of parts in one whole, not in all the bars.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Which improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is cut into 5 equal parts, so each part is 15. Count the shaded parts: 8. So it is 85. The denominator is the number of parts in one whole, not in all the bars.

items.q: Each circle is 1 whole. Which improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each circle is cut into 4 equal parts, so each part is 14. Count the shaded parts: 9. So it is 94. The denominator is the number of parts in one whole, not in all the circles.

items.q: Each circle is 1 whole. Which improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each circle is cut into 3 equal parts, so each part is 13. Count the shaded parts: 7. So it is 73. The denominator is the number of parts in one whole, not in all the circles.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Which mixed numeral is shaded?
items.e: 2 bars are full, so that is 2 wholes. 3 quarters more are shaded. So it is 2 34 (= 114).

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Which mixed numeral is shaded?
items.e: 2 bars are full, so that is 2 wholes. 2 thirds more are shaded. So it is 2 23 (= 83).

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Which mixed numeral is shaded?
items.e: 1 bar is full, so that is 1 whole. 2 fifths more are shaded. So it is 1 25 (= 75).

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Which mixed numeral is shaded?
items.e: 3 bars are full, so that is 3 wholes. 1 half more is shaded. So it is 3 12 (= 72).

items.q: Each circle is 1 whole. Which mixed numeral is shaded?
items.e: 1 circle is full, so that is 1 whole. 2 quarters more are shaded. So it is 1 24 (= 64).

items.q: Each circle is 1 whole. Which mixed numeral is shaded?
items.e: 3 circles are full, so that is 3 wholes. 1 third more is shaded. So it is 3 13 (= 103).

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. The shaded part is 2 13. Which improper fraction is that?
items.e: Each whole is 33. 2 wholes = 2 × 3 = 6 thirds. Add 1 more: 6 + 1 = 7. So 2 13 = 73.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. The shaded part is 1 35. Which improper fraction is that?
items.e: Each whole is 55. 1 whole = 1 × 5 = 5 fifths. Add 3 more: 5 + 3 = 8. So 1 35 = 85.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. The shaded part is 1 14. Which improper fraction is that?
items.e: Each whole is 44. 1 whole = 1 × 4 = 4 quarters. Add 1 more: 4 + 1 = 5. So 1 14 = 54.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. The shaded part is 2 12. Which improper fraction is that?
items.e: Each whole is 22. 2 wholes = 2 × 2 = 4 halves. Add 1 more: 4 + 1 = 5. So 2 12 = 52.

items.q: Write 134 as a mixed numeral.
items.e: How many 4s go into 13? 3 × 4 = 12, so there are 3 wholes. 13 − 12 = 1 left over. So 134 = 3 14.

items.q: Write 113 as a mixed numeral.
items.e: How many 3s go into 11? 3 × 3 = 9, so there are 3 wholes. 11 − 9 = 2 left over. So 113 = 3 23.

items.q: Write 2 45 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 55, so 2 wholes = 2 × 5 = 10 fifths. Add 4: 10 + 4 = 14. So 2 45 = 145.

items.q: Write 3 12 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 22, so 3 wholes = 3 × 2 = 6 halves. Add 1: 6 + 1 = 7. So 3 12 = 72.

sets.title: Fractions and mixed numerals on number lines from 0 to 3

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give a fraction.
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. The arrow is 3 marks after 0. So it shows 34.

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give a mixed numeral.
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. The arrow is 1 mark after 1. So it shows 1 14 = 54. It is not 1.4: the 4 means quarters, not tenths.

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give a mixed numeral.
items.e: Each whole is split into 2 equal parts, so each mark is 12. The arrow is 1 mark after 2. So it shows 2 12 = 52. It is not 2.2: the 2 means halves, not tenths.

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give a mixed numeral.
items.e: Each whole is split into 5 equal parts, so each mark is 15. The arrow is 2 marks after 1. So it shows 1 25 = 75.

items.q: Which letter shows 1 24?
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. For 1 24, go to 1, then 2 more marks. That is letter D.

items.q: Which letter shows 53?
items.e: Each whole is split into 3 equal parts, so each mark is 13. 53 = 1 23: go to 1, then 2 more marks. That is letter C.

items.q: Which letter shows 1 15?
items.e: Each whole is split into 5 equal parts, so each mark is 15. For 1 15, go to 1, then 1 more mark. That is letter B.

items.q: Which letter shows 1 13?
items.e: Each whole is split into 3 equal parts, so each mark is 13. For 1 13, go to 1, then 1 more mark. That is letter A.

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give a mixed numeral.
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. The arrow is 1 mark after 2. So it shows 2 14 = 94. It is not 2.4: the 4 means quarters, not tenths.

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. The arrow is 3 marks after 2. So it shows 2 34 = 114. Count all the marks from 0: 11.

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is split into 3 equal parts, so each mark is 13. The arrow is 2 marks after 2. So it shows 2 23 = 83. Count all the marks from 0: 8.

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is split into 5 equal parts, so each mark is 15. The arrow is 4 marks after 1. So it shows 1 45 = 95. Count all the marks from 0: 9.

items.q: Which letter shows 74?
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. 74 = 1 34: go to 1, then 3 more marks. That is letter D.

items.q: Which letter shows 2 15?
items.e: Each whole is split into 5 equal parts, so each mark is 15. For 2 15, go to 2, then 1 more mark. That is letter C.

items.q: Which letter shows 85?
items.e: Each whole is split into 5 equal parts, so each mark is 15. 85 = 1 35: go to 1, then 3 more marks. That is letter B.

items.q: Which letter shows 54?
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. 54 = 1 14: go to 1, then 1 more mark. That is letter A.

items.q: Which improper fraction is between 2 and 3 on a number line?
items.e: 2 = 84 and 3 = 124. 114 is between them (= 2 34). 74 is less than 2, 134 is more than 3, and 84 is exactly 2.

items.q: A number line from 0 to 3 is split into fifths. How many marks after 0 is 2 15?
items.e: Each whole has 5 marks. 2 wholes = 2 × 5 = 10 marks. 1 more mark: 10 + 1 = 11 marks. So 2 15 = 115.

items.q: Which number is closest to 2 on a number line?
items.e: Count the quarter marks from 2: 2 14 is 1 mark away, 1 24 is 2 marks away, 2 34 is 3 marks away and 1 14 is 3 marks away. So 2 14 is closest.

items.q: On a number line, which number comes just before 2 when you count by thirds?
items.e: Counting by thirds: 1 13, 1 23, 2. So 1 23 comes just before 2. 2 13 comes just after 2.

items.q: The school track is 14 km around. Ethan runs 5 laps. How far does he run?
items.e: Count by quarters: 14, 24, 34, 1, 1 14. 5 quarters = 54 = 1 14 km. It is not 1.4 km: the 4 means quarters, not tenths.

items.q: The track is 14 km around. How many laps does Jack need to run to go 2 km?
items.e: 4 laps make 1 km (4 quarters = 1 whole). 2 km = 2 × 4 = 8 laps.

items.q: Mia’s scoop holds 13 cup of flour. She puts in 4 scoops. How much flour is that?
items.e: Count by thirds: 13, 23, 1, 1 13. 4 thirds = 1 13 cups.

items.q: A recipe needs 2 cups of flour. Oliver only has a 12 cup measure. How many times must he fill it?
items.e: 2 halves make 1 cup, so 2 cups = 2 × 2 = 4 half cups.

items.q: At footy, the coach cuts oranges into quarters. The team eats 9 quarters. How many oranges is that?
items.e: 4 quarters make 1 orange. 9 = 4 + 4 + 1, so 9 quarters = 2 oranges and 1 quarter = 2 14 oranges.

items.q: Charlotte has 5 water bottles. Each bottle holds 12 L. How much water is there in all?
items.e: Count by halves: 12, 1, 1 12, 2, 2 12. 5 halves = 2 12 L.

items.q: Jack counts the distance as he runs 14 km laps: 14, 24, 34 … What does he say next?
items.e: 34 + 14 = 44, and 44 is 1 whole. So he says 1 km. 45 is a mistake, and 1 must not be skipped.

items.q: Isla cuts 7 pieces of ribbon. Each piece is 13 m long. How long are they all together?
items.e: 3 thirds make 1 metre. 7 = 3 + 3 + 1, so 7 thirds = 2 13 m.

items.q: A jug holds 2 L of juice. Mei pours 3 cups of 14 L each. How much juice is left in the jug?
items.e: Count back by quarters from 2: 1 34, 1 24, 1 14. 1 14 L is left. 34 L is what she poured.

items.q: Amelia reads for 14 of an hour each night. How long does she read in 6 nights?
items.e: Count by quarters: 14, 24, 34, 1, 1 14, 1 24. 6 quarters = 1 24 = 1 12 hours.

items.q: Oliver runs 7 laps of a 14 km track. Harper runs 1 12 km. Who runs further?
items.e: 7 quarters = 1 34 km. 1 12 = 1 24. 3 quarters is more than 2 quarters, so Oliver runs further.

items.q: Chloe needs 1 12 cups of flour. She uses a 14 cup measure. How many scoops does she need?
items.e: 1 cup = 4 quarters and 12 = 2 quarters. 4 + 2 = 6 scoops.

items.q: A 3 km bike path has a sign every 12 km. There is a sign at the finish but not at the start. How many signs are there?
items.e: Count by halves: 12, 1, 1 12, 2, 2 12, 3. That is 6 signs.

items.q: At a class party, each cake is cut into thirds. The students eat 8 thirds. How many cakes is that?
items.e: 3 thirds make 1 cake. 8 = 3 + 3 + 2, so 8 thirds = 2 23 cakes.

items.q: Kai counts by quarters. He says, “2 14, 2 24, 2 34, 2 45.” What should he say after 2 34?
items.e: 2 34 + 14 = 2 44 = 3. The denominator stays 4, so 2 45 is wrong.

items.q: A recipe says 94 cups of milk. Sienna pours 2 14 cups. Is that the right amount?
c: No. 94 is less than 2
No. 2 14 = 214
Yes. 2 14 = 94
No. 2 14 = 34
items.e: 2 wholes = 8 quarters. Add 1 quarter: 8 + 1 = 9. So 2 14 = 94. Yes, it is right.

items.q: Ava has run 1 34 km on a 14 km track. How many laps has she run?
items.e: 1 km = 4 laps. 34 km = 3 more laps. 4 + 3 = 7 laps.

items.q: Noah needs 3 cups of flour. He has put in 2 13 cups with a 13 cup scoop. How many more scoops does he need?
items.e: Count on by thirds from 2 13: 2 23, 3. That is 2 more scoops.

items.q: Matilda walks 1 14 km to school. Her brother says that is 1.4 km. Which is true?
c: 1 14 km is more than 1.4 km
1 14 km is the same as 1.4 km
1 14 km is less than 1.4 km
items.e: 1 14 is 1 whole and 1 quarter. A quarter is 25 hundredths, so 1 14 = 1.25. 1.4 is 1 and 4 tenths = 1.40. So 1 14 km is less than 1.4 km.

items.q: Grace fills cups of 15 L from a 2 L bottle of water. How many cups can she fill?
items.e: 5 fifths make 1 L. 2 L = 2 × 5 = 10 cups.
